J.  2024 BIANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT, JANUARY 1, 2024 TO JUNE 1,
  2024

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER thanked staff for adding the new “action notes” column
to the report as discussed.

Code Compliance Officer Hall explained that the biannual report is a snapshot of open cases
between January 1, 2024 to June 1, 2024, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
SCHACHTER.

Code Compliance Officer Hall explained that it is not typical to follow up with the reporting
party after the case is closed, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired about a case specific case on the report where the City
was denied access to a property.

  MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  LOS ANGELES COUNTY DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL
  MUNICIPAL SERVICES AGREEMENT RENEWAL

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
JUNE 11, 2024
   Recommendation: That the City Council approve the renewal of the Municipal
  Services Agreement with the Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care and
  Control.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Discussion ensued about the fact that the rates have not yet been provided by the County, and
the consideration of approving the contract without the set rates to avoid service disruption.

City Manager Grammer stated that staff shares the Council’s concern and explained that staff
has requested the new rates numerous times, hence the delay in bringing the contract renewal
to City Council for approval. He further noted that other contract cities are in the same position
and have taken this renewal to their City Councils for approval without having the new rates
from the County to ensure no disruption in service.

City Attorney Davis noted there is a 60-day termination provision if there was an extraordinary
increase after contract approval.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE THE RENEWAL OF THE MUNICIPAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
  WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL CARE AND
  CONTROL.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

B.  RESOLUTION NO. 2572 - APPROVING A FIVE-YEAR AGREEMENT WITH THE
  COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES FOR PUBLIC SERVICES PROVIDED BY THE LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY SHERIFF’S DEPARTMENT AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY
  MANAGER TO PROCURE SERVICES OF THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY SHERIFF’S
  DEPARTMENT ANNUALLY UP TO AN AMOUNT AUTHORIZED IN THE CITY’S
  OPERATING BUDGET FOR THE PERIOD OF JULY 1, 2024 THROUGH JUNE 30,
  2029

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) adopt Resolution No. 2572 approving the
  Municipal Law Enforcement Services Agreement between the County of Los Angeles
  and City of Rolling Hills Estates; 2) Authorize the Mayor to execute the 5-Year
  Agreement on behalf of the City; and 3) Authorize the City Manager to procure
  services of the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department up to an amount authorized
  in the City’s annual Operating Budgets for the Period of July 1, 2024 through June
  30, 2029.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Discussion ensued regarding the indemnity and liability section of the agreement.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA stated she was pleased to learn the indemnity and liability
issues were still being negotiated.

MAYOR SCHMITZ praised the Sheriff’s deputies who serve the City with the Lomita Station
but expressed frustration with the County’s contract process.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JUNE 11, 2024
   1) ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2572 APPROVING THE MUNICIPAL LAW
  ENFORCEMENT SERVICES AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE COUNTY OF
  LOS ANGELES AND CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES; 2) AUTHORIZE
  THE MAYOR TO EXECUTE THE 5-YEAR AGREEMENT ON BEHALF OF
  THE CITY; AND 3) AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO PROCURE
  SERVICES OF THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY SHERIFF’S DEPARTMENT
  UP TO AN AMOUNT AUTHORIZED IN THE CITY’S ANNUAL OPERATING
  BUDGETS FOR THE PERIOD OF JULY 1, 2024 THROUGH JUNE 30,
  2029.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

C.  FOUNDERS PARK PROJECT - REQUEST TO PURCHASE PLAY EQUIPMENT AND
  PARK FIXTURES FROM COLUMBIA CASCADE AND BUSCH SYSTEMS FOR
  PHASE 2

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize staff to purchase the Founders
  Park’s play equipment and fixtures from Columbia Cascade Company in the amount
  of $40,254.76, and two multi-bin waste receptacle units from Busch Systems, in the
  amount of $5,715.04, for a total of $45,969.80.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public Works Director Wahba outlined the details of the play equipment, which will blend in
with the natural surroundings, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

Public Works Director Wahba confirmed all plans are ADA compliant, in response to MAYOR
PRO TEM STEGURA.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE STAFF TO PURCHASE THE FOUNDERS PARK’S PLAY
  EQUIPMENT AND FIXTURES FROM COLUMBIA CASCADE COMPANY IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $40,254.76, AND TWO MULTI-BIN WASTE RECEPTACLE
  UNITS FROM BUSCH SYSTEMS, IN THE AMOUNT OF $5,715.04, FOR A
  TOTAL OF $45,969.80.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

D.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF MAY 21,
  2024: FOUNDERS PARK SIGNAGE

  Recommendation: That City Council approve the proposed signage language and
  Sample #3 to be installed at Founders Park adjacent to a centralized park bench.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas explained that staff developed the samples and
provided them to the Park & Activities Commission for review and feedback, in response to
COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JUNE 11, 2024
   APPROVE THE PROPOSED SIGNAGE LANGUAGE AND SAMPLE #3 TO BE
  INSTALLED AT FOUNDERS PARK ADJACENT TO A CENTRALIZED PARK
  BENCH.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

City Attorney Davis followed up on COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF’s inquiry about the code
compliance case in item 5J and explained that some cases require a court-ordered inspection
warrant in order to gain access for inspections.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the Cal Cities Los Angeles County Division General
meeting last week at the Los Angeles Air Force Base where she was elected to be Vice
President of the Los Angeles Division.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA attended the Clean Power Alliance (CPA) Board meeting
Thursday, and the South Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG) Steering
Committee meeting yesterday.

MAYOR SCHMITZ reminded the community to remove all sitting water to minimize
mosquitos.

MAYOR SCHMITZ reported on the Pano AI Wildfire Camera press conference in Rancho
Palos Verdes.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA stated that she and COUNCILMEMBERS HUFF AND
SCHACHTER attended the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce’s Street Fair
last weekend.

A.  AUTHORIZATION TO ATTEND THE CAL CITIES' ANNUAL CONFERENCE AND
  EXPO IN LONG BEACH, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 16-18, 2024

  CONSENSUS OF THE CITY COUNCIL TO ALLOW ANY/ALL COUNCIL
  MEMBERS TO ATTEND.

None.
